title: Migration demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood (API, Console, Optimize)
header:
Date: 2026-06-12 08:32 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Product), Nia Gomez (Solutions Eng), Priya Rao (Pavo Head ML), Marcus Bell (Infra), Liam Osei (Security), Product PM (unnamed)
Links shared: migration-mapping-v1.xlsx (drive link), redwood-security-deck.pdf (shared), benchmarks-spreadsheet.csv
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Pavo Health through a migration demo showing API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, Console walkthrough for routing/rollouts and Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for hybrid sensitive PHI-related workloads. Security/QoS questions raised (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Agreed next steps: bench run, security docs, pilot plan and pricing.
topics: Parity mapping (API/params/response streaming), embeddings migration, function/tool calling equivalence, console for model routing and rollouts, Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, KV caching, quantization), Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, security/KMS and audit logs, timeline and pilot checklist
action_items: Alex Chen (Redwood) - Share migration-mapping-v1.xlsx and sample request/response mappings by 2026-06-16
Samira Patel (Redwood SE) - Schedule benchmark run (latency + cost) and share results spreadsheet by 2026-06-19
Jordan Lee (Redwood Product) - Provide draft canary rollout config for Pavo's traffic patterns by 2026-06-18
Priya Rao (Pavo) - Provide representative prompt set and embedding corpus by 2026-06-15
Liam Osei (Pavo Security) - Confirm compliance checklist items (SOC2 scope, KMS requirements) by 2026-06-20
next_steps: Redwood to run a 24-hour benchmark against customer's sample prompts (OpenAI vs Redwood parity)
Customer to sign NDA addendum to share PHI-adjacent data for bench

transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're running about 50 minutes, we'll start with a quick migration overview then Sam will demo the API and Console.
[00:18] Priya: Sounds good, we primarily want parity with our current OpenAI and Anthropic stacks, and low friction migration ideally.
[00:26] Samira (SE): Great, we'll show mapping for requests, response shapes, streaming, and embeddings. quick note: some auto-transcribe words might flip Redwood product names, sorry in advance.
[00:45] Marcus (Infra): Quick ask \u2014 latency targets: we need p95 < 200ms for short completions, embeddings can be batch processed. Do you have numbers?
[00:58] Samira (SE): We do, we have benchmark sheets \u2014 I'll run your prompt set for both OpenAI and Redwood Dedicated and share the CSV. typically hosted api p95 for small models is ~120-180ms depending on region, dedicated can be better but also depends on GPU type and seq length.
[01:20] Priya: Are there differences in tokenization or embeddings dimensionality we need to be aware of coming from Anthropic?
[01:29] Samira (SE): Good question. For embeddings we support the standard float32/float16 outputs, and our embeddings map 1:1 in shape to the Anthropic/OpenAI vectors for their common models; we'll include a parity mapping in the spreadsheet. sometimes names differ \u2014 e.g., Anthropic's ctx param vs Redwood's context_length \u2014 but semantics are preserved.
[01:55] Speaker 1 (Product PM): Do you support function calling like OpenAI?
[02:02] Nia (Solutions Eng): Yes, function/tool calling is supported, streaming tool outputs are supported too. we demoed a quick function call implementation with structured json responses. small caveat: the SDK has different call signatures \u2014 we'll provide code snippets.
[02:25] Liam (Security): On data residency and KMS, can you run in our VPC and integrate with our KMS/HSM? We need to ensure customer-managed keys and logs for audits.
[02:38] Alex (AE): Absolutely \u2014 Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and audit logs. we'll share the security deck after this call.
[02:50] Marcus: Any SOC2/ISO stuff to see?
[02:53] Alex: We have SOC2 Type II in our standard hosted offering and enterprise packages include SOC2 evidence and ISO guidance; we'll attach the compliance pack.
[03:10] Samira: I'm going to share my screen \u2014 starting with the API parity doc. so on the left column you see the OpenAI request example: model, temperature, max_tokens, stop sequences. on the right is Redwood's mapping: model_alias, temp, token_limit, stop_tokens. code snippets for node/python included.
[03:36] Samira: note: streaming semantics are nearly identical \u2014 chunked events with deltas. there are minor differences in the field names: 'choices' vs 'outputs' in our responses in older versions, but current API supports both compatibility flags.
[04:05] Priya: That compatibility flag \u2014 is it opt-in? we have a lot of existing clients hitting OpenAI response shapes.
[04:12] Samira: yes it's opt-in per route; you can set compatibility_mode: openai in the Console and it rewrites the response envelopes.
[04:28] Alex: This is where Redwood Optimize comes in \u2014 we can suggest batching and caching settings that preserve your p95 SLO while reducing token cost.
[04:37] Priya: Can you explain KV cache? we saw that term in the docs.
[04:42] Samira: KV cache is our prefix cache mechanism \u2014 if you have repeated prefixes the runtime caches KV layers to avoid re-computation. it reduces tokens and latency for interactive flows. it'd help for your chatbot sessions with repeated system prompts.
[05:06] Marcus: For embeddings, do you support streaming and incremental indexing? we use Pinecone today but open to switching if indexing flow is simpler.
[05:15] Nia: We integrate with vector stores \u2014 we can bulk export embeddings and we support batched embedding APIs. incremental indexing is supported via our SDK with idempotent upserts. we'll include sample code for Pinecone and Milvus in the repo.
[05:40] Speaker 1: How about pricing \u2014 cost per token? migrating cost model is a big factor.
[05:46] Alex: We'll share pricing tiers \u2014 hosted per-token, dedicated reserved capacity and private licensing. For migrations we often do a hybrid pilot on hosted to get quick parity then shift to Dedicated for predictable throughput.
[06:02] Priya: Any gotchas with prompt engineering differences across vendors? we rely on Anthropic constraints for helpfulness/safety.
[06:11] Samira: We provide safety and output controls \u2014 you can apply filters and RLHF-safety layers. Anthropic-style constitutional constraints can be approximated via system prompt templates plus Redwood safety hooks. we'll include guidance.
[06:30] [Samira shares code snippet visible] "// OpenAI style" then "// Redwood mapping" \u2014 you can see doc links in chat.
[06:55] Priya: Could you show a live example of switching an existing OpenAI call to Redwood?
[07:01] Samira: Sure. here's an OpenAI fetch example -> simple find/replace: base_url, API key header, model mapping. in our example we swap model: "gpt-4o-mini" to model_alias: "rw-gpt4o-mini-v1", and set compatibility_mode. response body is nearly identical.
[07:28] [00:07:28] Marcus: latency looks similar in this demo, but what about long context windows and KV cache tradeoffs?
[07:34] Samira: KV cache helps with long context by caching prefix states, but you trade memory for speed. our Optimize tool will suggest quantization profiles if you want to reduce memory footprint with minimal quality loss.
[07:50] Priya: Quantization \u2014 does Redwood provide INT8 or other lower-precision runtime?
[07:56] Samira: Yes, we support multiple quantization profiles \u2014 INT8 and hybrid FP16/INT8 pipelines. Optimize will recommend profiles per model and your workload characteristics.
[08:12] Liam: For audit we need end-to-end logs. how detailed are the traces?
[08:17] Jordan (Product): Console provides per-request traces, token-level cost breakdowns, model version, and rollout tag. audit logs with S3 export are available for Private.
[08:30] Priya: Regarding model variants \u2014 if you fallback to smaller model in overload, does output semantics change drastically? we worry about hallucination differences.
[08:40] Samira: We recommend A/B testing via canary rollouts first; the Console supports weighted routing. Optimize also provides quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to your eval prompts so you can detect regressions fast.
[08:58] [08:58] Alex: I'm going to switch to Console to show model routing.
[09:03] Alex: On the left is your routes page, we can pin a route to a particular model_version or set an automatic fallback to a compatible variant. here's how to set a canary at 10% traffic.
[09:22] Priya: Nice, can we route by region too? some EU traffic needs EU-only models.
[09:28] Alex: Yes, region routing policies are supported. you can set rule-based routing (latency, cost, region, customer tier).
[09:40] Marcus: For Dedicated capacity \u2014 how is autoscaling handled?
[09:45] Jordan: Dedicated pools have configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. you'll set a min/max GPU count and we have policies for spike handling; we also support overprovisioning for predictable SLOs.
[09:58] Marcus: Any upgrade/downtime for model rollouts?
[10:02] Jordan: Canary rollouts and automatic fallback keep traffic safe. rollouts are config-only; underlying infra can be drained gracefully to avoid downtime.
[10:15] Priya: On the SDK side, our teams use python and node \u2014 how heavy is the migration work?
[10:21] Samira: Usually a few days for an initial switch if you use compatibility_mode. full optimization (batching, KV cache, quant profiles) takes additional tuning over 2\u20134 weeks.
[10:34] [10:34] Speaker 1: Are there any known incompatibilities with token counting and billing reconciliation? we saw token counts differ slightly across vendors.
[10:43] Alex: Tokenization differences exist; we provide tokenizers and token-count APIs to reconcile bills during migration. we'll include a reconciliation worksheet in the mapping doc.
[10:58] Priya: Could you walk through Optimize suggestions for our chat workload?
[11:03] Samira: Sure \u2014 based on your sample prompts we'd recommend batching embeddings with batch size 64 for throughput, prefix KV caching for chat, and INT8 quant profile for assistant model to save memory. expected savings estimate in the mapping doc.
[11:30] Marcus: For PHI-adjacent data we likely need Private deployment, can you do hybrid where some requests go to Hosted and sensitive traffic routes to Private?
[11:40] Jordan: Yes that's supported \u2014 you can route by tag or header; sensitive routes can be pinned to Private nodes in your VPC.
[11:52] Liam: For KMS integration \u2014 can we bring our own HSM?
[11:56] Alex: Yes, customer-managed KMS and HSM is supported in Private. we'll enumerate supported providers in the security deck.
[12:10] [12:10] Samira: quick demo \u2014 here's a sample canary config and a rollout graph. notice the regression alert triggers if eval scores drop by more than threshold.
[12:28] Priya: Eval scoring \u2014 is that out-of-the-box or do we upload our own eval set?
[12:33] Nia: Both. there are default metrics but you can upload your prompt set and ground truth; the system will run periodic evals.
[12:45] Speaker 1: For the bench run, can you mimic our traffic pattern? we have spikes at 9am daily.
[12:52] Samira: We'll parameterize the bench to use your traffic curve. please share the sample trace and we will replay it in the Dedicated and Hosted environments.
[13:06] [13:06] Alex: small thing \u2014 compatibility flags can be set per-route so developers don't need to rewrite clients during initial pilot.
[13:16] Priya: Good. What about rate limits and quotas? we have dozens of internal clients.
[13:22] Jordan: Per-route quotas and token-based rate limiting are available. you can set app-level and token-level policies.
[13:33] Marcus: Could you expand on caching TTLs and invalidation? we need near-real-time updates to documents.
[13:39] Samira: KV cache TTLs are configurable; for near-real-time you'd set shorter TTLs or disable caching for those routes. we can also implement cache invalidation hooks from your indexer.
[13:58] [13:58] Liam: Security question \u2014 do you log prompt text by default? we need selective redaction.
[14:04] Alex: By default, logs include metadata; full payload logging can be toggled and redaction hooks are supported. Private deployments can enforce stricter retention policies.
[14:18] Priya: Any portability concerns if we later want to self-host models entirely?
[14:23] Jordan: We offer on-prem packages; model artifacts are standard formats and runtime can run in your clusters. there is some ops work but it's a supported path.
[14:36] Speaker 1: Ok, can we see a quick embedding migration example?
[14:40] Samira: demo: OpenAI embedding POST -> Redwood embeddings/batch with vector_id, metadata. small field name changes but payload is same. list of upsert examples provided.
[14:56] Priya: Are embeddings deterministic between vendors? we saw slight drift.
[15:01] Samira: There will be numeric differences; we focus on semantic parity. the bench will measure retrieval recall against your ground truth.
[15:18] [15:18] Alex: circling back to timeline \u2014 you mentioned wanting a pilot within 3 weeks?
[15:23] Priya: yes, ideally a week of bench then a 2-week pilot.
[15:29] Samira: That's doable \u2014 we'll need your prompt set and access for benching.
[15:34] Marcus: About uptime SLAs for Dedicated, what are standard numbers?
[15:38] Jordan: SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated is usually 99.9% with options for higher tiers in enterprise contracts.
[15:48] Liam: For legal/procurement \u2014 are there standard enterprise terms?
[15:52] Alex: We have standard enterprise addendums; procurement can start after pilot signals.
[16:05] Priya: Any live issues migrating streaming chats historically? we have long streams with intermediate tool calls.
[16:11] Samira: Streaming with tool calls is supported; you'll want to test intermediate state save/restore for really long sessions. we have examples of KV checkpointing.
[16:28] [16:28] Speaker 1: Ok let's summarize next steps.
[16:31] Alex: Recap \u2014 Redwood will share migration-mapping doc, security deck, and run bench with Priya's samples. Pavo provides prompt set and confirms data sharing legal. Then we run 24h bench and follow with pilot.
[16:49] Priya: Fine. Also we need an estimate of cost delta if we flip to Dedicated.
[16:55] Alex: We'll provide a cost model in the pricing doc.
[17:03] Marcus: Can you include a sample canary policy and monitoring playbook?
[17:07] Jordan: Yes, adding that to action items.
[17:14] Liam: Security checklist required for our procurement.
[17:17] Alex: We'll attach the checklist to the security deck share.
[17:25] [17:25] Samira: I'll kick off the bench once we get the prompt set and credentials (read-only).
[17:31] Priya: We'll get the data to you by end of week.
[17:36] Alex: Great \u2014 thanks all, we'll follow up with notes.
[17:40] [End of recording]
